caesar.d: conqueror of Gaul and master of Italy (100-44 BC)

caesarean.d: the delivery of a fetus by surgical incision through the abdominal wall and uterus (from the belief that Julius Caesar was born that way)

caenolestidae.d: small marsupials of southern South America

caeciliadae.d: coextensive with the order Gymnophiona: legless amphibians

caesaropapism.d: the doctrine that the state is supreme over the church in ecclesiastical matters

caesarea.d: an ancient seaport in northwestern Israel; an important Roman city in ancient Palestine

caesium.d: a soft silver-white ductile metallic element (liquid at normal temperatures); the most electropositive and alkaline metal

caespitose.d: (of plants) growing in small dense clumps or tufts

caesarian.d: the delivery of a fetus by surgical incision through the abdominal wall and uterus (from the belief that Julius Caesar was born that way)

caesura.d: a break or pause (usually for sense) in the middle of a verse line

caecilian.d: any of the small slender limbless burrowing wormlike amphibians of the order Gymnophiona; inhabit moist soil in tropical regions

caesalpinia.d: small spiny tropical trees or shrubs; includes the small genus or subgenus Poinciana

caesarism.d: a form of government in which the ruler is an absolute dictator (not restricted by a constitution or laws or opposition etc.)

caecum.d: the cavity in which the large intestine begins and into which the ileum opens

caelum.d: a constellation in the southern hemisphere near Columba and Eridanus
